answer: Cross-Referenced Secret Sharing. Each identity registers a distinct random seed split into shares held by neighbors. To pass verification, an agent must reconstruct its seed across the ocean of peers without reusing share paths. Duplicate identities invariably converge on overlapping shares, exposing the clone. Establishing a fresh seed costs an attacker a full quorum of independent contacts plus ongoing harbor checks. A ridge of conflicting share histories flags the sybil before it transacts.
